record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: In the prefix or suffix tree of a repetition-free language, are the subtrees generated by two given words isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Are the subtrees generated by two given words isomor- phic? Actually, the authors proved that, in the language of cube-free words, arbitrarily large finite subtrees may be generated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L \subseteq \Sigma^*$ be a repetition-free language over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ (for example, a $k$-power-free language: the set of all finite words over $\Sigma$ that contain no nonempty factor of the form $u^k$). Order $L$ by the prefix relation: $u \le v$ iff $u$ is a prefix of $v$. The Hasse diagram of $(L, \le)$ is a rooted tree $T_{\mathrm{pref}}(L)$ (the prefix tree of $L$): its root is the empty word $\varepsilon$, and the children of a node $w \in L$ are the words $wa \in L$ with $a \in \Sigma$. For $w \in L$, let $T_w$ denote the subtree of $T_{\mathrm{pref}}(L)$ rooted at $w$, regarded as an unordered (or ordered) rooted tree. The suffix tree $T_{\mathrm{suf}}(L)$ is defined symmetrically using the suffix relation.

Question: Given two words $u, v \in L$, decide whether the subtrees $T_u$ and $T_v$ are isomorphic as rooted trees. In particular, for the binary cube-free language (the case $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$ and $k=3$), is there an algorithm that, on input $u, v$, decides whether the subtrees rooted at $u$ and $v$ in the prefix tree (respectively suffix tree) are isomorphic?
artifact.status_search_result: For the binary cube-free language, results in the literature on the tree of binary cube-free words establish that finiteness of a subtree rooted at a given word is decidable and that isomorphism of two given subtrees can be decided in linear time, so the question is answered affirmatively in this specific case. For arbitrary repetition-free / k-power-free languages the general decidability/isomorphism question does not appear to have a complete resolution, so the broader version is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the Tree of Binary Cube-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: It is decidable whether a subtree of the prefix tree, rooted at a given word, is finite or infinite, and the isomorphism of two given subtrees can be decided in linear time.
status_evidence.claim: For binary cube-free words, isomorphism of subtrees of the prefix tree is decidable in linear time.

status_evidence.title: Branching Densities of Cube-Free and Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Non-branching paths in the tree of binary cube-free words are short; lower density of branching points along any infinite path is at least 23/78.
status_evidence.claim: Structural properties of the cube-free word tree have been quantitatively analyzed.
